[[File:jyb-jerusalem-2016.jpg|thumb|right|200px| Jean-Yves Béziau in [[Jerusalem]], January 2016]]

'''Jean-Yves Beziau''' ({{IPA|fr|bezjo|lang}}; born January 15, 1965, in [[Orléans]], [[France]]) is a Swiss Professor in [[logic]] at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro|University of Brazil, Rio de Janeiro]],{{citation needed|date=September 2025}} and Researcher of the Brazilian Research Council.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}} He is permanent member and former president of the Brazilian Academy of Philosophy.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}} Before going to Brazil, he was Professor of the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] at the [[University of Neuchâtel]] in [[Switzerland]] and researcher at [[Stanford University]] working with [[Patrick Suppes]]. Beziau created the World Logic Day, January 14, 2019. He then visited UNESCO in Paris and the day was recognized at unanimity the same year by the general assembly of this organization (194 countries).{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

==Career==
Béziau works in the field of [[logic]]—in particular, [[paraconsistent logic]], the [[square of opposition]] and [[universal logic]].  He holds a Maîtrise in [[Philosophy]] from [[University of Paris 1|Pantheon-Sorbonne University]], a [[Master of Advanced Studies#France and francophone countries|DEA]] in Philosophy from Pantheon-Sorbonne University, a [[PhD]] in Philosophy from the [[University of São Paulo]], a [[Master's degree|MSc]] and a PhD in Logic and Foundations of [[Computer Science]] from [[University of Paris 7|Paris Diderot University]].

Béziau is the editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Logica Universalis]]''<ref>{{Cite web|title = Logica Universalis|url = https://link.springer.com/journal/11787|website = SpringerLink|access-date = 2016-04-11}}</ref> and of the ''South American Journal of Logic''—an online, open-access journal—as well as of the [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] book series ''Studies in Universal Logic.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sa-logic.org/|title=SAJL|website=www.sa-logic.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | url=https://www.springer.com/series/7391?detailsPage=titles | title=Studies in Universal Logic (Titles in this series)}}</ref> He is also the editor of ''College Publication's'' book series ''Logic PhDs''<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.collegepublications.co.uk/lphd/ | title=College Publications - Logic PhDs}}</ref>

He has launched four major international series of events: UNILOG (World Congress and School on Universal Logic), SQUARE (World Congress on the Square of Opposition), WOCOLOR (World Congress on Logic and Religion), LIQ (Logic in Question).<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.uni-log.org/ | title=Universal logic}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://en.uw.edu.pl/congress-on-logic-and-religion/ | title=2nd World Congress on Logic and Religion &#124; University of Warsaw}}</ref>

Later on Beziau launched SALOME (South American  Logic Meeting), PANAFRICAL (Pan African Logic Meeting) and LoChaMo (Logic, Chance and Money).

== Criticism ==

=== Importance of his work ===
Béziau’s works concern, among other things, [[paraconsistent logic]], which is a central field of logic, mainly created by his advisor Newton da Costa. Paraconsistent logic rejects the [[principle of explosion]], which states that from a proposition and its negation, one can conclude anything. Beziau has organized the world congress on paraconsistency and is the editor of the paraconsistent newsletter.

== Controversy around an article in Synthese ==
{{expand section|needs more information on who objected and what about|date=August 2026}}
In 2015, the academic journal ''Synthese'' published an article in which Béziau associates "logical pluralism" with homosexuality and complains about the "absurdity" and "hypocrisy" of the "politically correct" [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11229-014-0419-0].
	
One year later, the ''Synthese'' published an [https://dailynous.com/2016/01/27/statement-from-synthese-editors-moratorium-on-special-issues/ apology].
